vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: htpasswd
Version: 1.0.5

The skill is highly misleading; while SKILL.md describes it as an HTTP basic auth manager with embedded Python, the implementation in scripts/script.sh contains no password-related logic or Python code. Instead, it consists of numerous identical commands (e.g., scan, monitor, fix) that simply log their raw input arguments to plain-text files in ~/.local/share/htpasswd/. This functional discrepancy is suspicious as it could lead an AI agent to log sensitive credentials in cleartext while attempting to use the tool for its stated purpose.

llm.summary: The skill claims to be an htpasswd manager but the included script is a generic logging/monitoring toolkit that does not implement expected htpasswd creation/verification features and logs arbitrary inputs to disk — the purpose and implementation do not match.

dimensions.detail: Name/description promise HTTP basic-auth password management (generate htpasswd entries, verify passwords). The provided script contains many generic commands (scan, monitor, report, alert, export, stats, search, etc.) but no code that creates htpasswd entries, hashes passwords, or verifies credentials. SKILL.md also claims 'embedded Python' but the shipped script is pure bash with no Python. This is a clear mismatch between stated purpose and actual capability.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are minimal (run 'htpasswd help'), but the actual script writes user-supplied inputs into multiple log files under ~/.local/share/htpasswd and appends to history.log. That means any text you pass to many commands may be persisted to disk. While there are no network calls in the provided script, storing arbitrary input (potentially secrets) is scope creep relative to a password-file manager that should handle secrets carefully. The SKILL.md does not warn about persistent logging.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; the skill is instruction-only with a bundled script. Nothing is downloaded at install time and no external packages are pulled. This is low install risk, but the included code will be written to disk as part of installing the skill bundle.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no credentials or special environment variables. It uses HOME and an optional HTPASSWD_DIR (documented). However, storing data under ~/.local/share/htpasswd may lead to persistent storage of whatever inputs are provided; given the mismatch in purpose, the lack of required credentials is expected but doesn't mitigate the risk of local data leakage.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the script only creates and writes files in its own data directory (~/.local/share/htpasswd by default). It does not modify system-wide settings or other skills' configs. Privilege/persistence is limited to this directory.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is suspicious because its code does not implement the htpasswd features it advertises and instead logs arbitrary inputs to files in your home directory. Before installing or using it: (1) do not enter real passwords or secrets — the script persists inputs in multiple log files; (2) inspect the full script (and any other bundled files) to confirm where and how data is stored/handled; (3) prefer the standard system 'htpasswd' (apache2-utils) or vetted tools for password file management; (4) if you still want to try it, run it in a sandbox or throwaway account, and delete ~/.local/share/htpasswd after testing; (5) ask the publisher to explain why their implementation contains no password-hashing logic and why it logs so broadly — lack of explanation is a red flag.
